title: docs(charters): gate verdicts for a head go to the builder together, parser changes carry a generated probe, equivalence needs a differential probe, and repo lessons have a home

evidence.value: shell-doors took three security rounds until a generated pair probe closed the class (findings line 4); quality arrived after the fix commit (line 6); both cost gate rounds under G-1.
evidence.time: shell-stdin and records are guard-parser builds in this pass; their builders and gates should read the probe rule first.
evidence.risk: This pass found the shell-doors quality claim that five OPS alternatives were equivalent wrong for three of them; it would have opened a misparse had it been built as stated.
evidence.size: Six short rules over four charters, then `bin/wuwei agents build`; no runtime lines.

promise: Six charter rules from the findings and this pass. (1) planner.md: the planner forwards every gate verdict for a head to the builder together, once the last gate for that head returns, and the builder starts fixing only then. (2) _gate.md: when a change makes more commands unreadable or rewrites a parser, the gates probe the checks that do not rely on door words (the leak check on network programs, the infra ask) with the new shape. (3) builder.md and _gate.md: a change to guard parsing comes with a generated combinatorial probe run under real bash with a stub program on PATH (operator or spelling classes x positions x targets), and the PR or verdict reports how many commands were generated, how many really ran the door program, and the holes; a gate round on a parser re-runs it and adds a class for each hole it finds. (4) _gate.md: a gate calls code equivalent or deletable only after a generated differential probe between the head and the change shows 0 differences; a surviving mutant alone is reported as untested. (5) steward.md: a lesson about one repository's code goes in that repository's standards lines (.wuwei/standards.md); a lesson about how seats work in any repository is a charter proposal for the retro. (6) builder.md and _gate.md: probe fixtures that hold JSON escapes are written by code (json.dumps or a Python literal), never typed into a shell. Then `bin/wuwei agents build` regenerates agents/ and the vendored copies. Files: charters/planner.md, charters/_gate.md, charters/builder.md, charters/steward.md, agents/ and the vendored charters and agents under .claude/wuwei/. Runtime lines: 0, budget 0. Order: none; it can run beside free-lines-4 (no shared file), and it is best merged before shell-stdin's build starts. Rollback: revert the commit. Outside: the Stop hook wording (with the parent session's #1099) and the #1078 attestation path.
acceptance: given the branch head, when `bin/wuwei agents build` runs, then git status shows no change, and the suite's drift test passes

given agents/builder.md and agents/sentinel-security.md at the head, when a reader looks for the parser rule, then each names a generated combinatorial probe under real bash with a stub on PATH and the three counts it reports (generated, ran, holes)

title: fix(guards): a shell fed its commands on stdin and a named-fd redirect meet the doors

evidence.value: A stub git on PATH shows bash runs git push origin main for {fd}>x git push origin main, bash <<< 'git push origin main' and echo 'git push origin main' | bash; guards.bash at 9d6701e passes all three, and a generated probe finds 586 holes among 803 shapes that really run the push.
evidence.time: Open on main since before #1109; G-2 is dated 2026-10-23.
evidence.risk: Closes the push and ledger door bypass class for stdin-fed shells; the spike shows 0 holes of 803 for one line.
evidence.size: One runtime line and one regex edit in the spike; tests and fixture rows.

promise: A shell that reads its commands from stdin or a file, and a redirect on a named fd, meet the doors. (1) In guards._unwrap, sh, bash, zsh or dash with no -c body (fed by a pipe, a here-string, -s or < file, or given a script path) leaves the unread segment beside its own, so the existing multi-line or unreadable rule refuses the command when its raw text names a door program; a command naming none still passes. (2) In guards.segments, a {name} glued before a redirect operator at the start or after a separator ({fd}>x, {a_b}<x) is dropped the way an fd number is, so the program after it is read. Files: cli/wuwei/guards.py, tests/test_guards.py, tests/fixtures/routes.json, the vendored guards.py, and docs/site/concepts/doors.md if it lists the unreadable shapes. The builder runs a generated combinatorial probe under real bash: fd spellings ({fd}, {a_b}, {A1}, {_}, 3, 10) x redirect operators x targets x positions (start, end, after ;, after &&, after |, inside ( )), and shells (bash, sh, dash, /bin/bash, env bash, command bash) x flags (none, -s, -e, -x) x feeders (<<< glued and spaced, a pipe, |&, 0<<<) x both quotes; holes must be 0. Rollback: revert the commit. Outside: a script file that holds a door command while the command line names none (bash run.sh: the guard is not a sandbox), and heredocs, which the multi-line rule already refuses. Assumptions: no recorded seat route pipes text naming a door program into a shell (the suite's seat-command corpus passed under the spike); overturned if a corpus row moves from pass to refuse.

title: fix(guards): a help request passes the doors, and an --input file's head, base and body are read as JSON

evidence.value: guards.bash at 9d6701e refuses gh pr merge --help, gh pr merge -h, gh pr merge 5 --help, gh pr ready --help, gh pr create --help, git push --help and git push origin main --help; the live door refused `gh pr merge 5 --help` during this pass.
evidence.time: A false refusal, not a bypass; seats meet it when they read help.
evidence.risk: Loosens a door, so the parser reading -h and --help must follow pflag exactly (`gh pr merge 5 -t --help` gives --help to -t and merges).
evidence.size: About three lines in gh_command, _api and the git branch of bash.

promise: A help request passes the doors, and an --input file's head, base and body are read as JSON. (1) gh pr merge, create, new, ready and edit with -h or --help as pflag reads them through guards._flags (anywhere before --, alone or in a short cluster, --help=true) print help and run nothing, so the guard passes them. A word pflag gives to a valued flag is not help: `gh pr merge 5 -t --help` still meets the merge door, and so does `gh pr merge 5 -- --help`. (2) git push with -h or --help, as git's option parser reads them, passes the push door. (3) For gh api --input, when the file parses as a JSON object, head, base and body are read with json.loads, so \u and \n escapes decode as gh sends them; a file that is not valid JSON keeps today's reading. Files: cli/wuwei/guards.py, tests/test_guards.py, tests/fixtures/routes.json and the vendored guards.py. Runtime lines: estimate +3, budget 5. Order: after records, because both edit the git branch of guards.bash. Acceptance comes from real execution: real gh against a fake host through gh's http_unix_socket setting shows which requests a help spelling sends, and real git against a local bare remote shows no ref was pushed. The builder runs a generated probe of help spellings (-h, --help, --help=true, --help=false, -dh, -h=x) x subcommands (merge, create, new, ready, edit) x positions (before and after the number, after each valued flag, after --), compared with what real gh sends to the fake host; mismatches must be 0. Probe fixtures that hold JSON escapes are written by code. Rollback: revert the commit. Outside: gh help subcommands other than gh pr, and `--input` read from stdin (still refused as unreadable for graphql). Assumptions: git push --help and -h after positionals show help and push nothing (parse-options); overturned if the bare-remote test shows a push, in which case (2) covers only the spellings shown to push nothing.
acceptance: given real gh configured with http_unix_socket to a fake host that logs every request, when it runs each of `gh pr merge --help`, `gh pr merge 5 --help`, `gh pr ready -h` and `gh pr create --help`, then the fake host logs no write request, and given each command, when guards.bash reads it, then it passes
given the same fake host, when real gh runs `gh pr merge 5 -t --help` and `gh pr merge 5 -- --help`, then the guard sends each to the merge door (refused while the PR's evidence has gaps)

given a local bare remote and a clone with a commit on main, when real git runs `git push origin main --help` and `git push origin main -h` from the suite, then the bare remote has no main ref, and guards.bash passes both; `git push origin main` is still refused

given an --input file written by json.dumps with head 'feature', base 'ma\u0069n' and a body whose WUWEI-Item line is escaped, when guards._api reads it, then head, base and body equal the decoded strings
why: A small false-refusal fix seen live in this pass; it waits behind records only because both edit the same branch of guards.bash.

title: fix(evidence): owner review reads only owner review rulings, and the CI-not-started read covers docs-only diffs, an unreadable Actions host and pull_request_target
